note: Current version. v2 fixes a structural deadlock found by Muse in review the same day: in an audit_required task the audit GUARD refuses every step validation until the audit step is done, while start_work_order/request_slot/validate_done all require a step depends_on to be fully done - so an audit step WITH a depends_on edge can never start and its predecessors can never validate. The audit step therefore carries depends_on [] in v2; the guard itself is the gate. Same defect exists in programming-build v2 (audit depends_on [test_execution]) and is the headline fix of its v3 rebuild. Dag sha256 b0d5f94f1cef507839f7932ef35685b2990fcccdaa81814fa3c8bd64f14c7b3f.

step_dag.name: plan: fit check and instance record
step_dag.acceptance: plan records: the request and the requester; the fit check against list_templates/get_template with its outcome (new template / new version of an existing template / already covered - a covered outcome ends the instance here with the finding recorded); the spec manifest artifact path; any standing gate touching template work, quoted from the gates record

step_dag.name: interview: zero in on the workflow
step_dag.acceptance: every topic answered by the requester or explicitly waived with a reason: purpose; trigger; inputs; outputs; step list with owners; dependency gates; acceptance evidence per step (artifact + store + probe where possible - a worker's success claim is not evidence); failure modes; shared-resource and serialization constraints; probe candidates; surfaces touched (banks via their per-bank MCP entries, tools, files). Answers land in the spec manifest artifact AND as a comment on this task. While answers are outstanding the step stays open with the questions cited in its comment - a cited wait, not a stall. Drafting does not start before this step validates

step_dag.name: verify premises against their stores
step_dag.acceptance: every premise in the spec manifest that names existing state (templates, banks, services, files, constants) is verified against its store and quoted in the evidence; constants are read from the store as text, never transcribed from a screenshot or summary; a premise the store contradicts is surfaced as a breakpoint, not carried into the draft

step_dag.name: draft the template version
step_dag.acceptance: draft artifact carries the full step_dag in registry shape (key / name / owner / acceptance / depends_on per step) plus version metadata: plan step first (3.3); step keys kebab-case and treated as permanent (a later version may not drop a key with live instances); every owner a real seat, orchestrator only for the closed list in AGENTS.md 3.7, execution steps naming the seat that holds their work orders; depends_on acyclic; per-step acceptance checkable from the store; probe declarations recorded for probeable checks (6.6 D1); class-crossing closures named with their token-argument path; serialization constraints from the interview encoded as dependency gates or serial steps; the audit_required decision recorded with its reason

step_dag.name: audit the draft (non-author)
step_dag.acceptance: the auditor checked the draft itself, not a summary: owners real and locus-correct (3.7); DAG acyclic and plan-first; every acceptance checkable and evidence-shaped; probes declared where a check is mechanical; class-crossing paths named; no scratch-template dry-run in the design (the registry has no delete); key stability against any prior version; a rejection carries a fix path (6.6C) and the bounce is counted on the step (bound 3, 6.6A) The audit gate is carried by the tool's audit guard, not by a depends_on edge: in an audit_required task an audit step WITH dependencies deadlocks the task (no step validates before the audit, and the audit's own work cannot start before its dependencies validate). This step therefore carries no depends_on; its work order is created by choreography once the draft exists, and the audit is worked against the draft artifact itself.

step_dag.name: requester approval gate
step_dag.acceptance: the requester's ruling on the audited draft is recorded as a comment quoting it verbatim with its timestamp; no approval, no seed; the workflow waits on this gate without looping. If the workflow changes behavior surfaces (rules, prompts, skills), its text routes through a behavior-change instance - this workflow seeds template mechanics only

step_dag.name: seed the template version
step_dag.acceptance: create_template (new template) or add_template_version (revision) executed with the approved dag; the tool's return and the seeded dag's hash are recorded on the task; list_templates shows the template at the seeded version

step_dag.name: dry-run on a trivial instance, self-cleaning
step_dag.acceptance: the seeded version is instantiated as a task on a trivial but real-shaped instance; at least one work order is carried through the full choreography (request_slot, spawn on the granted node, bind_slot, structured propose_done carrying any declared probe, executor verdict, accept, validate_done); render_composition of the instance is attached to this task as the DAG proof; the dry-run instance is then closed or cancelled with its reason IN THE SAME RUN - no board or registry debris. On failure: findings recorded, and draft-audit-review-seed re-run for version+1 as recorded deviations (6.6E)

step_dag.name: close with the dual write
step_dag.acceptance: closing comment carries: template name and version, the dag hash, the dry-run instance id and its verdict, every deviation, and the closing retain's id (retain into bank kurisu through the hindsight entry, 3.4). If the template becomes a standing workflow, a behavior-change instance for the AGENTS.md 6.6E template-list update is boarded and its id recorded here - boarded, not bundled
